comment: Reviewed availability metadata for the Mathematical Symbols catalog.
Each MathJax TeX symbol map is attributed to the LaTeX capability that actually
provides those commands. 'core' means the LaTeX kernel or base math mode needs no
\usepackage. A null package means MathJax implements the construct itself and LaTeX
does not: those records are excluded from the catalog with a manifest reason rather
than being offered as insertable LaTeX.
'verified' means the attribution was reviewed by hand against the package's own
documentation. Everything else stays unknown, and the panel shows it as unknown
rather than as available.
Provenance: the map names are MathJax's own (mathjax-full 3.2.2,
js/input/tex/<config>/<Config>Configuration.js), which is also the licence-bearing
source of the symbol data itself. See vendor-licenses/.

Physics-characters.note: Internal re-mappings of |, ) and ]; not insertion items.

action-macros.note: MathJax accessibility extension; LaTeX has no equivalent.

colorv2.note: MathJax compatibility shim for the old color extension.

remap.note: Internal character remapping, not a command.

not_remap.note: Internal character remapping, not a command.

letter.note: Internal tokeniser class, not a command.

digit.note: Internal tokeniser class, not a command.

command.note: Internal tokeniser class, not a command.

special.note: TeX syntax characters, not insertable commands.

text-special.note: TeX syntax characters in text mode, not insertable commands.

comment: What a loaded package also brings with it.
MathematicalSymbols.md §6: 'Model known transitive capabilities in reviewed
metadata.' Without this, a document that loads amssymb is told it cannot
typeset \mathbb — because \mathbb is attributed to amsfonts and the package
list literally says 'amssymb'. The probe in the built application found
exactly that.
The edges are LaTeX Workshop's own, from the bundled
src/renderer/data/latex-workshop/packages/*.json `deps` arrays, copied here
rather than read at runtime: the data store loads those files lazily and the
panel needs one synchronous answer. Only the packages this catalog can name
are listed.
A conditional dependency is deliberately omitted rather than included
unconditionally. xcolor pulls colortbl only with the `table` option and
mhchem pulls pgf/tikz only with an `arrows=` option, so claiming them always
would say a package is loaded when it may not be — the one direction of
error this feature must not make.

unimathsymbolsPackages.comment: Package names that appear in unimathsymbols.json's free-text detail field. Reviewed against the package's own documentation; 'verified' false keeps the requirement visible as unknown.
